components.gap: Preserve the source variants of this entry's definitions (Durrett sec. 1.1, pp. 1 and 4). Durrett defines a sigma-field as a nonempty collection closed under complements and countable unions, without listing Omega as a member, and gives his reason for leaving closure under countable intersections out of the definition (the shorter list is easier to check); he defines an algebra, or field, as a collection closed under complements and pairwise unions and obtains closure under intersection by De Morgan's identity. The routed definition (measurable-probability.tex lines 25-47) gives only its own form (a collection containing Omega), with no statement of the source form or proof of the equivalence, no synonym field for an algebra and no stated reason; no routed file supplies them.

components.gap: Supply the source variant of this entry's subadditivity item: Durrett's Theorem 1.1.1(ii) (p. 2) states subadditivity in covering form, mu(A) <= sum over m of mu(A_m) whenever A is contained in the union of the A_m. The routed theorem (measurable-probability.tex lines 111-113; annex lines 47-58) states and proves only the union form mu(union of A_n) <= sum of mu(A_n); the covering form, which bounds a set by a strictly larger cover, is neither stated nor derived anywhere on the route.
